question: Do Democrats win control of the US Senate in the 2026 elections
quote: So you guys have almost talked me out of it. But I'm going to be wildly optimistic and say 49% odds.
turn_text: So you guys have almost talked me out of it. But I'm going to be wildly optimistic and say 49% odds. North Carolina is gone. Ohio seems like it's gone. I was talking to a consultant the other day who felt good about it. But there's been no indication that I'm aware of in the public polling that Brown's not ahead. So that would be two. I don't know. There are just so many jump balls. I was heartened by the Fox poll that had Paxton tied with Tallarico. But the subsequent polling is back to Tallarico nearly ahead. But my most likely path is I guess everyone else's. North Carolina, Ohio, Alaska, Texas. And I just – I guess I'm thinking maybe one of these red states just kind of tilts towards the GOP and keeps it from happening and keeps it a tie. But who knows? We'll do more detailed.
host_quote: So Noah Rothman, X question to you. Percentage odds that Democrats take the Senate at this very moment.
resolution_criteria: Which party controls the US Senate after the 2026 elections, including any runoffs: Democrats if they and the independents who caucus with them hold at least 51 seats, or 50 with a Democratic vice-presidential tiebreak; otherwise Republicans. A YES answer means Democrats. Decided by the Associated Press's call. If AP has not called it within 60 days of election day, the certified official result decides. Resolves when control is called.
outcome_source_title: AP: Democrats took the Senate late Tuesday (control call explainer)
